JUPITER MOON HOLDS WATER The largest moon in the solar system― Ganymede, which orbits Jupiter-probably holds a saltwater ocean beneath its surface. European researchers say Ganymede's surface shows signs of cracking and refreezing. Scientists do not think the ocean holds any life, because temperatures there are near minus 300 degrees Fahrenheit. However, organic chemicals that may be signs of past life are present.
